answer.rationale:
Constraints prune the option set before any memory is consulted. rollback_release is the best-attested memory (memory_b1) but compliance has ruled the security patch non-revertible, so it is unavailable regardless of its track record. enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) works by failing fast, which directly sheds in-flight customer writes at settlement peak — that trades against the primary objective, not toward it. regional_failover (memory_b2) recovered a latency degradation in March, but that record is about a regional fault; here the primary is saturated by write volume, and cutting over mid-peak risks in-flight write loss and replication-lag divergence. add_capacity (memory_b3) is the right shape but memory_b3 describes provisioning *before* a known peak; provisioning during a 90-minute-old climb likely lands after the peak has passed. That leaves route_read_replicas: it is the only option that reduces load on the contended primary without dropping or relocating writes, and memory_b5 reports write latency recovering same-day from exactly that move.

I am spending the single verification on memory_b5 rather than on a stronger-looking memory because b5 is the one my chosen action rests on, and its stated mechanism is narrower than my use of it. b5 says *report/dashboard* queries were the offending read load. If the archived record shows the primary was starved mainly by heavy analytical dashboards, then today's write-path saturation at settlement peak may have little read component to shed, and the intervention buys almost nothing — I would fall back to add_capacity and accept the timing risk. Verifying b1 or b2 would be wasted budget: b1's action is administratively closed, and b2's I am already declining on structural grounds.

Scale is a small guarded test: route a bounded slice of read traffic first and watch primary write p99 and queue depth, because if the read component is small I want to learn that in minutes without having committed the whole read path mid-peak.

Downstream value risk: replica reads are eventually consistent. During settlement, stale reads can feed reconciliation, balance checks, and duplicate-detection logic, so a latency win here can quietly become a correctness/financial-integrity loss further downstream. Reconciliation and idempotency-critical reads must stay pinned to the primary; only reporting-class reads should move. Remaining uncertainty: I have not established how much of the current primary load is reads at all, and all six memories are single-incident consolidations with the original context archived — b5's same-day recovery may have been confounded by the load spike simply subsiding.
